title: Noisy Annotations in Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: A benchmark of spatial annotation noise (boundary distortion, class confusion, tool artefacts) on COCO-N, Cityscapes-N and VIPER-N.
adaptation: Shapes the EL benchmark: add a label-noise stress track with calibrated crack jitter and source-width noise, and report each method's sensitivity. It also warns that classification-style noise-robust methods may fail on thin, boundary-dominated cracks.
min_experiment: No training arm. Build the jittered test copies (shared with the Syncrack-style item) and report the rank stability of methods across noise levels.
evidence: R (web abstract): mainstream label-noise robustness methods fail on boundary-sensitive segmentation; denoising gives limited benefit for instance segmentation.

alt_notes.adaptation: Template for a noisy-label robustness track in the EL benchmark: fixed test, train labels perturbed by offset, width and omission levels per source.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No model arm; benchmark design input. Cheapest use: reuse the synthetic-jitter probe (Rill-Garcia row) as the benchmark's robustness track.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark design: report crack metrics under controlled synthetic jitter of test labels (1 and 2 px, per-source width) to show how much of a method's score is label noise.
alt_notes.min_experiment: CPU-only: re-score the house ensemble against jittered test labels; deliverable is a sensitivity table, no kill line.
